newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech closed-end fund Garant pegs yield to PX50.
newsitem.headline: Czech closed-end fund Garant pegs yield to PX50.

text.p: Garant, a new closed-end mutual fund managed by Komercni Banka a.s. unit Investicni Kapitalova Spolecnost KB, said it would tie members' potential yield to the development of the Czech capital market.

The fund's manager Otakar Hrazdira told a news conference on Monday that Garant would invest 80 percent of its assets in "riskless" fixed-income instruments and the rest would be placed in options on Czech shares held by foreign banks.
He said the two-year closed-end fund would guarantee a yield equal to 65 percent of the percentage increase in the official Prague Stock Exchange index, the PX50, during the period.
"The investors are guaranteed by contract a (pre-tax yield) amount of 65 percent from the potential growth of the PX50 index," Hrazdira said.
The fund will launch its two-year life span with the value of the PX50 index as an average of the five immediate business days ending on November 11
That value will be compared with the average of three-months of the PX50 ending November 30, 1998.
In the case of a drop in the PX50 at the end of two years, fund participants are guaranteed return of their entire investment but without yield, Hrazdira said.
Each certificate in the fund has a nominal value of 10,000 crowns and will be publicly tradable. Annual management fees are set at 1.5 percent of the year's average asset value.
